answer: New identities must finish a chain of six work proofs, each proof's input an echo of the previous output, so proofs cannot run in parallel. One proof costs 10 compute units and one epoch, so one fake costs 60 compute units plus a six-epoch delay before earning. One hundred fakes cost 6,000 compute units and still wait six epochs each, since extra machines cannot shorten a chain. Copying another identity's plume of proofs voids it and burns its deposit. Trust rises one layer at a time like a knoll.
